01.actor: A blind man who reviewed mishnayot before Mar Shmuel
01.event: The blind man was late, Mar Shmuel sent a messenger who missed him on the road and then reported that the blind man's wife had committed adultery.
01.turn: The blind man, who had not been at home, had to decide what to do on the word of a single messenger.
01.outcome: Mar Shmuel told him to divorce her if he trusted the messenger, and not to if he did not.
01.summary: A blind man who studied mishnayot with Mar Shmuel one day failed to arrive. Mar Shmuel sent a messenger after him. The two took different roads and missed each other, and the messenger reached the man's house. The messenger came back and said the man's wife had committed adultery. The blind man brought this to Mar Shmuel, who told him to divorce her if he trusted the messenger and not to if he did not.

04.actor: A man who came before Rabban Gamliel
04.event: A man told Rabban Gamliel he had found an unobstructed orifice on his wedding night.
04.turn: Rabban Gamliel suggested he had approached from a different angle and told a parable of a man groping in the dark who finds a door open only if he diverts.
04.outcome: Rabban Gamliel did not accept the claim at face value and offered his parable as the explanation (a second version has him say the man diverted deliberately).
04.summary: A man came before Rabban Gamliel and said he had found his bride's passage open. Rabban Gamliel asked whether he had approached from the wrong angle, and told him a parable: a man walking in the dark finds a door open if he pushes aside what blocks it, and locked if he does not. Some say instead that he asked whether the man had deliberately displaced the door and bolt.

05.event: Rav Pappa served drinks at his son Abba Mar's wedding and poured a cup for Rav Yitzhak son of Rav Yehuda, who did not stand before him.
05.turn: Rav Pappa was offended that he was not shown the respect due to him.
05.summary: At the wedding of his son Abba Mar, Rav Pappa was serving the guests drinks. When he poured a cup for Rav Yitzhak son of Rav Yehuda, Rav Yitzhak did not stand up for him, and Rav Pappa became angry.

06.event: They seized an orphans' cow from an alley over a debt and asked Rabbi Yohanan, who approved.
06.turn: Reish Lakish told them to return the cow, and they went back to Rabbi Yohanan.
06.outcome: Rabbi Yohanan said he could do nothing, since a colleague of his stature disagreed with him.
06.summary: Rabbi Yohanan's relatives seized an orphans' cow in an alley and Rabbi Yohanan told them they had seized it properly. They then went to Reish Lakish, who told them to give it back. They returned to Rabbi Yohanan, who said that since his equal disagreed with him he could not help them.

08.event: A man snatched a belt from her and, when she asked for it back, asked whether she would be betrothed to him if he gave it.
08.turn: She took the belt and said nothing.
08.outcome: Rav Nahman ruled she could say she merely took her own property, so her silence did not make a betrothal.
08.summary: A woman was selling belts when a man snatched one. She asked for it back and he asked whether she would be betrothed to him if he gave it. She took it and stayed silent. Rav Nahman ruled that she could say she had only taken her own property, so no betrothal resulted.

09.actor: Mar Yehuda, Rav Yosef and Rav Shmuel, and Rabba
09.event: Mar Yehuda met two colleagues at the study hall entrance and raised a proof from one baraita, then a contradiction from another.
09.turn: They had no answer and fell silent.
09.outcome: They brought the difficulty to Rabba, who dismissed it as the work of a quarrelsome person and resolved it by explaining the first baraita as dealing with an animal found to be a tereifa.
09.summary: Mar Yehuda found Rav Yosef and Rav Shmuel at the door of Rabba's study hall and cited a baraita from which he drew an inference about Rabbi Shimon. He then raised a second baraita that contradicted it, and they could not answer. They went to Rabba, who said a quarrelsome person had put them up to it and resolved the contradiction by limiting the first baraita to an animal found to be a tereifa.

10.event: Rav Giddel was negotiating to buy a plot of land and Rabbi Abba bought it first; Rav Giddel complained through Rabbi Zeira to Rav Yitzhak Nappaha.
10.turn: Rav Yitzhak Nappaha confronted Rabbi Abba with a parable of a pauper whose loaf is taken, and Rabbi Abba said he had not known.
10.outcome: Rabbi Abba refused to sell it but offered it as a gift; Rav Giddel would not take a gift and Rabbi Abba would not take the land, so it was called the land of the Sages.
10.summary: Rav Giddel was working to buy a plot when Rabbi Abba bought it. The complaint went from Rav Giddel to Rabbi Zeira to Rav Yitzhak Nappaha, who confronted Rabbi Abba at the festival. Rabbi Abba said he had not known and would not sell, since it was his first purchase, but would give it as a gift. Rav Giddel refused a gift and Rabbi Abba would not keep the land, so it became known as the land of the Sages.

11.actor: A yavam and yevama who both admitted no levirate marriage was consummated
11.event: They came before Rava, who ordered halitza for her.
11.turn: Rav Sherevya objected that a baraita requires both a bill of divorce and halitza.
11.outcome: Rava retracted his ruling on account of the baraita.
11.summary: A couple, a yavam and yevama, both admitted they had not consummated the levirate marriage and came before Rava. Rava told the Sages to arrange halitza for her. Rav Sherevya objected that a baraita requires a bill of divorce as well as halitza, and Rava answered that if it is taught, it is taught, retracting his ruling.

12.actor: A husband who collected his wife's inheritance, and Rabbi Ami
12.event: A man travelled with six hundred of his own dinars to collect his wife's four hundred in Bei Hozai and took one dinar of hers on the way back.
12.turn: The Rabbis objected to Rabbi Ami's ruling that the man had spent his money and eaten hers, saying he had consumed principal rather than produce.
12.outcome: Rabbi Ami replied that this made him one who spent and did not eat, who swears to what he spent and collects it.
12.summary: A woman inherited four hundred dinars in Bei Hozai. Her husband went and brought it back at a cost of six hundred of his own dinars, and used one dinar of hers on the way. Rabbi Ami ruled that what he spent and what he ate cancel out. The Rabbis objected that he had eaten principal, and Rabbi Ami answered that then he was one who spent without eating and may swear and collect his expenses.

13.actor: A maidservant of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi's household
13.event: She immersed in a ritual bath, and on coming out a bone was found between her teeth.
13.turn: The foreign object in her mouth put the validity of her immersion in doubt.
13.outcome: Rabbi required her to immerse again.
13.summary: A maidservant in Rabbi's household immersed herself ritually. When she came up, a bone was found between her teeth. Rabbi had her immerse a second time.
13.missing: The incident is cited only as an objection in a legal argument.

15.actor: A groom and bride before Rabban Gamliel bar Rabbi
15.event: The groom said he found no blood, and the bride said she was a virgin.
15.turn: Rabban Gamliel had the cloth brought, soaked and laundered it, and found drops of blood on it.
15.outcome: He told the groom to go take possession of his acquisition.
15.summary: A man came before Rabban Gamliel bar Rabbi and said he had found no blood on his wedding night, while his bride said she had been a virgin. Rabban Gamliel asked for the cloth, soaked it in water and washed it, and found drops of blood on it. He told the groom to go and take possession of his bride.

16.event: A narrow inlet of the sea breached a courtyard wall in a shepherds' village and the matter came before Rav Yehuda.
16.turn: The case seemed to conflict with Shmuel's other ruling requiring a majority of the wall or two boards.
16.outcome: Rav Yehuda required only one upright board to remain in order to permit the courtyard.
16.summary: In a shepherds' village an inlet of the sea cut through a courtyard and breached a whole wall. The case came before Rav Yehuda, who required only one standing board of wall to permit the courtyard. Rav Yosef cites this to Abaye, who answers that water is treated leniently.
16.missing: The incident is told briefly as a precedent in an argument.

17.event: A woman came before Ameimar asking for one-tenth of her father's estate, and her brothers said that if they had the money they would pay her off.
17.outcome: Rav Minyumi took his silence to show that Ameimar had retracted and treated the daughter as a creditor who can be paid in cash.
17.summary: Rav Minyumi was standing before Ameimar when a woman came asking for her one-tenth share of her father's estate. Her brothers said that if they had money they would pay her off. Ameimar said nothing, and Rav Minyumi took this to mean that Ameimar had retracted and now saw her as a creditor.
17.missing: The passage opens with Rav Ashi's opinion; the incident is cited as proof.

18.actor: Rabbi Yosei bar Avin (or Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Zevida, or Ameimar)
18.event: A visiting sage ruled on the children of a slave and a Jewish woman, once for an unmarried woman and once for a married woman.
18.turn: Rav Sheshet gave a different account of who ruled and how.
18.outcome: The reports conflict and the Gemara then states the law as fit in both cases.
18.summary: Ravina reports that when Rabbi Yosei bar Avin visited a town, he ruled the child of a slave and an unmarried woman fit and that of a married woman unfit. Rav Sheshet says it was another Rabbi Yosei who ruled both fit, and Rav Aha reports that Ameimar also ruled both fit.
18.missing: These are conflicting reports of rulings with no scene or detail, so there is no real story.

19.event: Rav arrived at Apsetaya and prohibited climbing even a tree stripped of its branches.
19.turn: This seemed to contradict the permission just stated.
19.outcome: The Gemara explains Rav found an unguarded field and fenced it in as a safeguard.
19.summary: Rav arrived in Apsetaya and forbade people to climb even a stripped tree. The Gemara says he found an unguarded field, meaning widespread transgression, and put a fence around it.
19.missing: It is a one-line precedent cited against a rule, with no scene or characters beyond Rav.

20.event: Rav Nahman found Rav Adda bar Ahava and his son-in-law Rav Hana in the Pumbedita marketplace posing challenges to each other about the mishna.
20.turn: Rav Nahman told them he thought even the deaf-mute brother's widow was uncertain.
20.outcome: He gave his own view and the exchange ends there.
20.summary: Rav Nahman came upon Rav Adda bar Ahava and his son-in-law Rav Hana sitting in the Pumbedita marketplace debating a mishna. They explained their limit for the rule and Rav Nahman answered that even in the deaf-mute brother's case it was still uncertain.
20.missing: The setting is a framing for a legal debate, with no event beyond the conversation.
